mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate investments, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals a weakening demand, which leads to reduced corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a strengthening supply side, which leads to increased economic activity and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months signals a stable monetary policy, which leads to increased investor confidence and risk-taking, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which leads to increased economic activity and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening supply side, which leads to reduced economic activity and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.
